reconstructed_theorem_text:
Measurable Omega with arbitrary measure mu and filtration F; initial scalar x; progressive scalar drift b; horizon T; accumulated process A.

x:Omega→R; b:[0,infinity)×Omega→R; T∈[0,infinity). mu is not assumed finite. lambda_t is Lebesgue measure on [0,t], represented on nonnegative reals.

Assumptions: x is strongly measurable with respect to F_0. b is strongly progressive for F. For mu-a.e. omega, b(·,omega) is integrable against lambda_T. No positivity assumption on T.

Conclusion: Define A(t,omega)=x(omega)+∫ b(s,omega) d lambda_t(s). Then A is strongly progressive for F. For every t≤T and every omega, A(t,omega)=x(omega)+∫ 1_{s<min(t,T)}b(s,omega) d lambda_T(s). For mu-a.e. omega, A(·,omega) is continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T].

Quantifier order: For every such x,b,T satisfying the assumptions, all three conclusions hold: progressivity globally; a deterministic all-omega identity for every t≤T; and path continuity plus bounded variation on [0,T] mu-a.e.

Scope: The prefix identity is pointwise for all omega, including exceptional nonintegrable paths, using Lean's total integral convention. Continuity and bounded variation are only almost sure. Progressivity is on all nonnegative times.

Constant dependencies: No existential constants.
